title: Are Chinese Firms Handing the United States Data?
gist: Deng Yuwen argues that Chinese AI firms such as Alibaba, Moonshot and DeepSeek, by distilling Anthropic's Claude at industrial scale, may be funneling large volumes of real Chinese user 'intent data' into U.S. systems, exposing a blind spot in China's cross-border data rules. Beijing faces a dilemma: shutting down distillation protects data but slows China's catch-up to U.S. frontier models.

insights.claim: An Anthropic report accused leading Chinese AI firms, including Moonshot AI and DeepSeek, of large-scale distillation of Claude, in one case routing at least 300,000 real user requests through the model over 10 days without users' knowledge.
insights.speaker: Deng Yuwen
insights.so_what: Distillation erodes U.S. frontier labs' moats and is likely to drive tighter API access controls and possible policy action.
insights.locator: A recent report by the U.S. artificial intelligence company Anthropic

insights.claim: Per Anthropic, Alibaba's distillation-related activity exceeded 151 million exchanges between May and July, Moonshot's exceeded 23 million, and DeepSeek conducted over 12.1 million exchanges in 14 days in July.
insights.speaker: Deng Yuwen
insights.so_what: Scale of reliance suggests Chinese model progress partly depends on U.S. model access, a vulnerability for Chinese AI valuations if access is cut.

insights.claim: China's cross-border data rules, including the Provisions on Promoting and Regulating Cross-Border Data Flow, target formal database exports and may have missed a new channel: AI firms using proxy accounts to feed real user requests into U.S. foundation models.

insights.claim: China faces a trade-off: allowing continued distillation of U.S. models leaks Chinese data, while cutting it off would require more compute, time and trial and error, slowing China's catch-up to U.S. frontier models and widening the gap.
insights.speaker: Deng Yuwen
insights.so_what: Any Chinese ban on distillation would be a relative positive for U.S. frontier labs' lead and a headwind for Chinese model makers.
